refutation_criterion_verbatim: Re-running the published rubric over the same frozen candidate snapshot yields a different ranking or verdict for any candidate, or any of the six mandated dimensions has no scoring rule a second party could apply.

step2_positive_control_defect_planted_sc.evidence: Two independent invocations of the defect-planted scorer over the identical frozen snapshot produced different SHA-256 hashes (1e185f5c99bf732f49389a47d73e98d99a87c0dad6fb44164b79ce5b9be353d7 vs 8a48c48aa4e3716e7228b867aba908473ed7c128e87e53e5c6397d88f05fa1be), because each call embeds its own wall-clock timestamp. The same two-replay check applied to the REAL scorer (step 1) found byte-identical hashes. This proves the two-replay gate has the power to catch a real non-determinism defect and did not simply pass because the check is toothless.
step2_positive_control_defect_planted_sc.how_planted: scorer_nondeterministic.py imports run() unchanged from scorer.py, then sets out['generated_at'] = time.time() before writing -- the ONLY difference from the real scorer.
step2_positive_control_defect_planted_sc.planted_defect: scorer_nondeterministic.py adds a time.time() 'generated_at' field to the output payload before serialization.

step3_independent_second_party_check.note: runC_independent.json was produced by independent_reference_check.py, which re-implements all six formulas directly from rubric.v1.json's tables and never imports scorer.py. Its byte-identical match to scorer.py's own runA.json demonstrates a second, independently-written code path applying only the published rubric document reaches the identical ranking -- i.e. the rubric's scoring rules are mechanically reproducible by a second party, not merely self-consistent within one implementation.
